original.title: fix: correct modified Huber loss gradient in `ml/incr/binary-classification`
original.body:
## Description

Fixes #13111. The `else` branch of `_modifiedHuberLoss` in `ml/incr/binary-classification`'s `Model` was missing a factor of `2` in the "quadratically smoothed" region, **and** was being applied unconditionally for `d = y*f(x) < 1` — including the `d >= 1` region, where the modified Huber loss (and therefore its gradient) is exactly zero.

This goes slightly beyond what #13111 literally flagged (just the missing `2`): I independently re-derived the three-region gradient against the cited references before changing anything, since applying *only* the factor-of-2 fix without also bounding the branch at `d < 1.0` would still be wrong for `d >= 1`.

Per the modified Huber loss definition ([Wikipedia, "Variant for classification"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huber_loss#Variant_for_classification); scikit-learn's [`_sgd_fast.pyx.tp` `ModifiedHuber.dloss`](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/main/sklearn/linear_model/_sgd_fast.pyx.tp)), the gradient of the loss w.r.t. the decision value `p = y*f(x)` is:

- `p >= 1`: `0`
- `-1 <= p < 1`: `-2*y*(1-p)`
- `p < -1`: `-4*y`

Since the weight update here is `w += eta * (-dloss/dp) * x`, the middle region needs `2*eta*(y - p*y)` (not `eta*(y - p*y)`), and the `p >= 1` region needs no update at all. The `p < -1` branch (`4.0*eta*y`) was already correct and is unchanged.

## Testing

Added three new test cases to `test/test.model.js` covering each region (`p < -1`, `-1 <= p < 1`, `p >= 1`), confirming:
- the factor-of-2 fix in the quadratic region,
- the model weight vector is left unchanged when `p >= 1`,
- the existing `p < -1` branch is unaffected.

```
$ node test/test.model.js
TAP version 13
# main export is a function
ok 1 ...
ok 2 main export is a function
# the modified Huber loss update includes a `2` factor when `-1 <= y*f(x) < 1` (see stdlib-js/stdlib#13111)
ok 3 includes the `2` factor in the update
# the modified Huber loss does not update the model weight vector when `y*f(x) >= 1`
ok 4 leaves the model weight vector unchanged
# the modified Huber loss update matches the existing `-4*eta*y` branch when `y*f(x) < -1`
ok 5 applies the unchanged `d < -1` branch

1..5
# tests 5
# pass  5
```

`eslint` on both touched files is clean (aside from a pre-existing, unrelated spelling warning on "pegasos").

original.title: zlib: reject reset while a zstd frame is incomplete
original.body:
Calling `reset()` on a zstd compressor while a frame is still in progress left
the stream in a state where it produced output that could not be decompressed,
without reporting anything. This makes `reset()` throw instead.

Fixes #66087.

### The problem

`reset()` drops the state of the frame currently being compressed. Any bytes
that were already written out — by `flush()`, or by an earlier `write()` that
filled the output buffer — cannot be taken back, so they stay at the start of
the output stream. The next frame is then appended to that fragment, and the
result decodes as corruption.

```js
stream.write(Buffer.from('hello'));
await new Promise((r) => stream.flush(r));  // emits 14 bytes, frame unfinished
stream.reset();                             // frame state dropped here
stream.end(Buffer.from('world'));           // emits another 14 bytes, new frame
// 28 bytes total: fragment + complete frame -> ZSTD_error_corruption_detected
```

Without the `reset()` the same input produces 22 bytes and decodes to
`helloworld`, because `end()` continues the existing frame (8 bytes) instead of
starting a new one (14 bytes).

zstd requires buffers to be fully flushed before a new compression job starts —
see `ZSTD_compressStream2` in `deps/zstd/lib/zstd.h`:

> Before starting a new compression job, or changing compression parameters, it
> is required to fully flush internal buffers.

`ZSTD_compressStream2` returns non-zero while a frame is unfinished, which is
how a caller is meant to detect this. The compressor context was not keeping
track of that.

### The fix

`ZstdCompressContext` now records whether the current frame has completed. A
frame is complete once `ZSTD_compressStream2` has been called with `ZSTD_e_end`
and returned 0. `ResetStream()` refuses with `ERR_ZLIB_INCOMPLETE_FRAME`
otherwise:

```text
Error [ERR_ZLIB_INCOMPLETE_FRAME]: Cannot reset a zstd stream with an incomplete
frame; end the frame or discard the output produced so far
```

This follows the existing behaviour for the other invalid reset case, where
`reset()` during a write already throws.

After the change the repro above reports the error instead of emitting a
corrupt stream.

### What is not changed

- `reset()` before any write still works.
- `flush()` followed by `end()` still works and still produces a valid stream.
- `reset()` on a finished frame is unaffected.

### Tests

`test/parallel/test-zlib-zstd-reset-incomplete-frame.js` covers the reset
mid-frame case, the valid `flush()` + `end()` sequence, and the valid
`reset()` before writing.

Ran against a `--debug-node --debug-symbols` build on Linux x86_64:

```text
$ ./out/Release/node --test test/parallel/test-zlib-zstd-reset-incomplete-frame.js
✔ ZstdCompress reset throws when a frame is incomplete
✔ ZstdCompress flush followed by end still produces a valid stream
✔ ZstdCompress reset before any write still works
ℹ pass 3
ℹ fail 0
```

Existing zlib tests:

```text
$ ./out/Release/node --test test/parallel/test-zlib-zstd.js \
    test/parallel/test-zlib-zstd-reset.js \
    test/parallel/test-zlib-zstd-flush.js \
    test/parallel/test-zlib-reject-garbage-after-end.js \
    test/parallel/test-zlib-zstd-pledged-src-size.js \
    test/parallel/test-zlib-zstd-dictionary.js
ℹ pass 19
ℹ fail 0
```

### Notes

gzip and brotli hit the same class of problem for the same call sequence (their
output is undecodable too). I kept this PR to zstd because that is where the
failure is completely silent, but I am happy to look at the other two codecs
separately if that is wanted.

original.title: build,src: gate jspi flag on V8_ENABLE_WEBASSEMBLY
original.body:
Since d937c8c6cd ("wasm: enable JSPI") ProcessGlobalArgsInternal()
unconditionally appends --experimental-wasm-jspi to the V8 argument
list. V8 only defines the experimental_wasm_* flags when it is built
with V8_ENABLE_WEBASSEMBLY, and configure --v8-lite-mode sets
v8_enable_webassembly=0. V8::SetFlagsFromCommandLine() is called with
remove_flags=true, which silently leaves unrecognized flags in argv, so
node reports "bad option: --experimental-wasm-jspi" and exits with
kInvalidCommandLineArgument. The first binary to run that code is
node_mksnapshot, so every --v8-lite-mode build has failed since
v24.20.0:

  bad option: --experimental-wasm-jspi
  node_mksnapshot failed with exit code 9

Forward v8_enable_webassembly to all targets as V8_ENABLE_WEBASSEMBLY,
the same way common.gypi already forwards the other V8 build flags, and
only push the JSPI flag when WebAssembly is compiled in.

Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/59941

original.title: textparse: validate numeric fields in OM2 composite values
original.body:
The OpenMetrics 2.0 parser reads a few numeric fields of composite values without checking them, and each one ends up as bad data rather than a parse error.

- `count` / `gcount` / `zero_count`: a native histogram takes the integer path whenever these are integral, so `count:-1` reaches `uint64(count)` and is stored as `18446744073709551611`. NaN and infinities do not survive that conversion either.
- Classic histogram `le`: the `strconv.ParseFloat` error was dropped, so an unparseable threshold was yielded as the label value. A `NaN` threshold also passed the ordering check, because every comparison with NaN is false, and then became `prevLe`, disabling the check for the rest of the buckets.
- Summary `quantile`: same dropped error, and no `[0.0, 1.0]` bound.

`-Inf` is now accepted as the first classic bucket threshold. The OM2 ABNF permits it (`ch-neg-inf-bucket`), but `prevLe` started at `-Inf` and the comparison was `<=`, so it was rejected.

One judgement call: `gcount` is validated together with `count`, although the review comment scoped that check to non-gauges. `isGauge` does not affect the float/int decision, so a gauge histogram reaches the same `uint64` conversion. Happy to narrow it.

Testing: new cases in `TestOpenMetrics2ParseErrors` and a parse test for the `-Inf` bucket, each failing without the parser change; `go test ./model/... ./scrape/...` passes.

#### Which issue(s) does the PR fix:

Part of #19745, items 6, 7 and 8. The rest of the list is untouched.

The OM2 parser has not shipped in a release yet, so there is no user-facing change.

comments.author: Suhail98
comments.body:
Pushed a revision after going back to the spec.

The first version rejected negative, NaN and infinite counts outright. The spec is more specific than that: a negative gcount is explicitly allowed, and NaN or infinite counts are only SHOULD NOT. So the check is now negative-only, and its justification is the model rather than the spec — `FloatHistogram.Validate` returns `ErrHistogramNegativeCount`, so a negative count cannot be stored either way. NaN counts already take the float form and are left alone, and infinite counts now take it too instead of wrapping through `uint64`.

comments.author: upramod
comments.body:
Shud we validate the bucket count here too? 

A value like bucket:[1.0:-1,+Inf:3] still parses successfully even though histogram bucket cnts are expected to be non-negative. 

Since this PR is tightening validation of the composite numeric fields, it seems worth rejecting negative bucket counts here as well and adding a test.

comments.author: dashpole
comments.body:
Finite floats `>= 2^64` (like `1e20`) also satisfy `count == math.Trunc(count)` and will overflow `uint64(count)` on the integer path. Since negative values are already rejected above, checking `>= float64(math.MaxUint64)` covers both `+Inf` and large finite values:
```suggestion
		count >= float64(math.MaxUint64) || zeroCount >= float64(math.MaxUint64) ||
```

comments.author: Suhail98
comments.body:
Correction to what I wrote above, after checking each input against `main` instead of reasoning from the code.

A negative count is not always ingested: `Histogram.Validate` catches the wrapped value whenever `sum` is a real number, though the error it gives blames the bucket totals. The silent case is a NaN sum, which relaxes that check to "count is at least the bucket total" — and a wrapped count always is. So the tests now use `sum:NaN`, which `main` accepts with no error at all, rather than the finite-sum variant that `main` already rejects for a confusing reason.

I also dropped the part that routed infinite counts to the float form. That would have newly accepted input the parser rejects today, and the spec only discourages infinite counts rather than forbidding them, so they are rejected with a clear message instead.

original.title: tsdb: fix appends after mmap-only recovery
original.body:
When recovery leaves a series with only memory-mapped chunks, the head appender treats it as a fresh series because `headChunks` is nil. Older samples pass Append validation and can then disappear at Commit. Conflicts against the latest stored timestamp also pass without the expected duplicate-sample error.

This fixes validation to consider mapped chunks and restores the last stored value once at the end of Head initialization for mmap-only series. The value is read from the mapped chunk: skipped WAL records may include conflicting samples that were never stored.

After recovery, older samples follow the existing out-of-order window rules, exact duplicates of the latest sample remain accepted, and conflicting values are rejected. New in-order samples still append normally. The change adds no per-series fields or append-time chunk decoding; initialization visits existing series and decodes the final chunk only for affected mmap-only series.

### Regression test

The test persists samples at timestamps 100 and 200, reopens a mmap-only series, then checks timestamps 150, 200 and 300. It covers both appender APIs, snapshot/no-snapshot recovery, all seven existing sample-type scenarios, and OOO disabled/within-window/outside-window. Queries verify accepted samples are stored. A conflicting WAL record verifies that recovery uses the stored value.

The first commit adds the regression test, which fails on the base. The second commit fixes the behavior. The fixture explicitly creates the mmap-only recovery state; this does not imply every normal restart reaches it.

### Validation

- All 84 regression cases fail on the unchanged upstream base and pass with the fix.
- `go test ./tsdb/... -count=1` passed.
- `go test -race -tags dedupelabels ./tsdb -run '^TestHeadAppendAfterMmapOnlyRecovery$' -count=1` passed.
- `make lint GOLANGCI_LINT_OPTS='--timeout 10m'` passed.

#### Which issue(s) does the PR fix:

Discovered while reviewing #19711. This fixes the pre-existing storage behavior independently of that statistics proposal.

#### Release notes for end users

```release-notes
[BUGFIX] TSDB: Correct out-of-order and duplicate-sample validation after recovery leaves a series with only memory-mapped chunks, preventing accepted out-of-order samples from being silently dropped.
```

## Bug

After WAL corruption repair, a series can retain its older memory-mapped chunks but have no current in-memory head chunk. In that state, a **new out-of-order sample within the configured acceptance window can pass `Append()` and `Commit()` successfully but never be stored**.

A concrete example:

```text
Mapped chunk:  100 → 1, 150 → 2
Head chunk:    200 → 3
```

If corruption prevents replaying the WAL record for timestamp 200, automatic repair discards that record and the subsequent WAL data. The mapped chunk survives, leaving samples at 100 and 150 but no head chunk. This PR reproduces that sequence using normal appends, normal chunk mapping, and automatic WAL repair. With an intact WAL, the control test rebuilds the head chunk normally. Production frequency has not been measured.

Now send `125 → 4`, with OOO enabled and timestamp 125 inside the configured window. It should be stored in an OOO chunk. Instead:

1. `appendable()` sees `headChunks == nil` and takes the fresh-series shortcut. It returns success with `isOOO=false`, without considering the mapped chunks.
2. `Commit()` repeats that validation and tries the in-order insertion path.
3. In-order insertion sees that 125 is at or below the last mapped timestamp, 150, and returns “not inserted.”
4. Commit treats that result as an exact duplicate, drops the sample, and returns success.

The same shortcut also skips value-conflict detection: `150 → 999` is silently dropped instead of being rejected as conflicting with the stored `150 → 2`.

## Fix and how it works

- **Only treat a series as fresh when both its head chunk and mapped chunks are absent.** Older timestamps then reach the existing OOO-window checks and are either routed to OOO storage or rejected under the configured rules.
- **Restore the cached last sample value for mmap-only series during initialization.** This lets validation distinguish an exact duplicate at the latest timestamp from a conflicting value. - **Also restore these values after successful automatic WAL/WBL repair.** Corruption makes `Init()` return early; the DB repairs the log and continues using the partially recovered head without calling `Init()` again.

This restores validation state. The head chunk remains absent until a newer in-order sample creates one. Mapped chunks remain immutable, and the low-level in-order timestamp guard remains in place. Exact duplicates of the latest stored sample remain accepted and deduplicated.

The low-level rejection was deliberate: the original mmap implementation refused older timestamps, and returning errors was explicitly [left as follow-up work](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/6679#discussion_r420197546). original.title: fix(remote-write): return 400 instead of 204 for duplicate labels in v1
original.body:
## What happens

A remote-write `WriteRequest` containing a series with the same label name twice (e.g., `dup_demo{zone="a", zone="b"}`) is answered `204 No Content`. Prometheus logs the problem, increments `prometheus_api_remote_write_invalid_labels_samples_total`, and stores nothing. The sender is told the write succeeded.

Remote-write 1.0 has no partial-success field, so the status code is the only signal a sender has — and here it says the opposite of what happened.

## Root cause

In the v1 `write()` method (line 180-183), when `HasDuplicateLabelNames()` detects duplicates, the code logs a warning and `continue`s to the next timeseries. The function returns `nil` (no error), so `Store()` returns `204 OK`.

By contrast, the v2 `appendV2()` method (line 348-349) correctly appends to `badRequestErrs` and ultimately returns `400 Bad Request`.

## Fix

Introduce `errInvalidV1Labels` sentinel error. When duplicate labels are detected in the v1 path, return this error instead of continuing. In `Store()`, add a case to check `errors.Is(err, errInvalidV1Labels)` and set `wr.SetStatusCode(http.StatusBadRequest)`.

This aligns v1 behavior with v2 and with the Mimir implementation which already returns 400.

```release-notes
[BUGFIX] remote-write v1: return 400 Bad Request when series contain duplicate label names
```

Fixes #19665

original.title: fix(sourcemap): skip URL source roots when injecting sources content
original.body:
## What

Fixes #23518.

`injectSourcesContent` misreads source maps whose `sourceRoot` is a URL.

`computeSourceRoute` tries `realpath(path.resolve(dirname(file), map.sourceRoot))`, which fails for a URL, so the root is treated as missing. The relative `sources` are then resolved with `path.resolve(sourcePath)` — against `process.cwd()` — and for a file inside `node_modules` that lands outside its package, producing:

```
Sourcemap for ".../node_modules/domutils/lib/esm/index.js" points to a source file outside its package: ".../index.ts"
```

Packages like `domutils@3` and `entities@4` publish maps with `"sourceRoot": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/…/src/"` deliberately, so devtools can fetch the original sources from the tag they were built from. `webpack://` roots take the same path. There is nothing local to read, and the package-boundary check is meaningless for a remote root.

This skips sources-content injection for maps with an external `sourceRoot`. The map is passed through unchanged, so other consumers keep resolving `sources` against the remote root.

## Reproduction

https://github.com/murugu-21/vite-url-source-root-repro- — pure `vite` (`createServer` + `ssrLoadModule` with `ssr.noExternal`), no test runner:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/murugu-21/vite-url-source-root-repro-.git
cd vite-url-source-root-repro-
npm install
npm run repro
```

## Tests

Two cases added to `packages/vite/src/node/server/__tests__/sourcemap.spec.ts`:

- a map with a remote `sourceRoot` is left untouched and does not warn;
- a map whose source genuinely resolves outside the package still warns.

`pnpm vitest run packages/vite/src/node/server/__tests__/sourcemap.spec.ts` passes (11 passed, 2 Windows-only skipped). The first case fails without the change.

original.title: fix(css): resolve relative imports in imported preprocessor files for lightningcss
original.body:
<!--
- What is this PR solving? Write a clear and concise description.
- Reference the issues it solves (e.g. `fixes #123`).
- What other alternatives have you explored?
- Are there any parts you think require more attention from reviewers?
-->

fixes #23508

## Problem

With `css.transformer: 'lightningcss'`, when a plain CSS entry imports a
preprocessor file (`.scss`/`.less`/`.sass`) from a different directory, relative
`@import`s inside that imported file are resolved relative to the **entry**
file's directory instead of the imported file's directory.

This happens because `compileLightningCSS`'s `resolver.read(filePath)` callback
passes the entry module `id` to `compileCSSPreprocessors` (and
`transformSugarSS`) instead of the imported `filePath`.
`compileCSSPreprocessors` sets `opts.filename = cleanUrl(id)`, which the sass/less
workers use as the base for relative import resolution
(`sassOptions.url = pathToFileURL(options.filename)`). So
`@import './_vars.scss'` inside an imported `box.scss` is rooted at the entry
`main.css`, producing `Error: Can't find stylesheet to import.`

The default postcss transformer is unaffected because `compileCSSPreprocessors`
is reached with the imported file's own path there.

## Fix

Pass `filePath` (the file being read) instead of the entry `id` in `resolver.read()`
for both the preprocessor and the SugarSS branch. When the entry *is* a
preprocessor file, `id === filePath`, so existing behavior is unchanged — this
only corrects the multi-file-import case. Using `filePath` also gives more
accurate sourcemap sources for imported files.

Verified against the repro in #23508: the build previously failed with
`Can't find stylesheet to import.` and now succeeds, producing
`.box{background:#6495ed}`.

## Alternatives explored

- Passing `filename`-style root only for preprocessors: unnecessary, `filePath`

fixes #23506

## Problem

`mergeConfig` (and normal config resolution via plugin `config` hooks) throws when merging a `server.hmr` object while `server.ws` is `false`:

```
TypeError: Property description must be an object: undefined
```

When recursion reaches `server`, `setupHmrWsOptionCompat` is called. If `server.ws === false` it returns early without installing the `hmr` `wsOptionKeys` accessors. When recursion later reaches `server.hmr`, the code copies those accessors with `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(defaults, key)!`, which is `undefined` in this case, so `Object.defineProperty(merged, key, undefined)` throws.

## Fix

Guard the descriptor copy in the `server.hmr` branch — only copy the accessor when it actually exists on the merged object. When `server.ws` is `false` there are no ws-related HMR options to forward anyway, so skipping them is the correct behavior.

I also added a regression test in `config.spec.ts` that merges `server.ws: false` with an `hmr` object on both sides and asserts no throw.

## Alternatives explored

- Installing the accessors even when `ws === false`: that would run `hmrWsOptionsDeprecationCall` for a config knob that has no effect (ws is disabled), so it felt misleading.
- Treating the whole `hmr` merge as a no-op when `ws === false`: too aggressive, the unrelated hmr options (like `hmr.overlay`) should still merge fine.

## Review notes

Nothing else changes: when `ws` is enabled the accessors exist and behave exactly as before, so this PR only affects the previously-crashing `ws: false` path.
